## Current CI/CD Shape

Tuturuuu currently automates:

- Vercel preview deployments for non-`production` branches
- Vercel production deployments from the `production` branch
- Independent Vercel preview and production deployments for satellite apps such as `apps/cms`
- Affected-app gating for Vercel deployments before dependency install, build, or deploy work
- Supabase staging migrations driven from `main` and production migrations driven from `production`
- Docker parity and image validation for the self-hosted web runtime
- Modal deployment for `apps/discord`
- Mobile build artifact generation
- Package publishing to npm
- Quality, lint, type, test, and security checks

## Important Repo Conventions

- For most authored changes, run the applicable check, lint, test, and build
  workflows in CI and verify their results on the exact commit. Focused local
  checks help find problems quickly but do not replace that CI evidence. If a
  workflow queue is demonstrably stuck, record the pending jobs and local
  results; resume the exact-commit CI checks before claiming release readiness.
- `ci-check.yml` reads `tuturuuu.ts` and can disable an individual workflow centrally.
- Vercel workflows use `tuturuuu.ts` app metadata and workspace `workspace:*` dependency closures to run only affected app deploys.
- `bun.lock` changes run all Vercel app deploys because lockfile ownership is ambiguous without a source or manifest path.
- Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs enabled workflows even when changed paths would otherwise be unaffected.
- Production Vercel workflows cancel superseded per-app runs only for newer
  `production` pushes. A `main` commit or manual recovery run never cancels an
  active production deployment.
- The external-app internal-package build uses the same cancel-superseded policy, so rapid pushes cannot finish as green no-op builds.
- Database migrations are not treated the same as app deploys; staging and production each have explicit prerequisite logic, with staging now sourced from `main`.
- Docker setup and image-build CI (`docker-setup-check.yaml`) are disabled, including manual dispatch, until explicitly resumed.

## Cross-app users-core regression tests

The canonical approval regressions live outside the package source tree:

- `packages/users-core/tests/approvals/get-tenant-boundary.test.ts`
- `packages/users-core/tests/approvals/review-reads-tenant-boundary.test.ts`

The source type-check project keeps `rootDir: "src"`. Vitest discovers the
cross-app tests separately through `packages/users-core/vitest.config.ts`;
relocating these tests does not expand the package's source compiler boundary.

That config maps the Web-specific imports `@/lib/post-email-queue` and
`@/features/reports/report-limits` to their exact `apps/web/src` files before
its default `@` alias, which still points to `packages/users-core/src`.
The exact `@tuturuuu/satellite/auth` mapping points to
`packages/satellite/src/auth.ts`; it keeps the satellite namespace separate
from the package-local `@` imports.

Run selected tests from `packages/users-core` with that canonical config and
the receiver's qualified dependencies. For a source `TS6059` error, check that
the cross-app test is outside `src`. For a Vitest module-resolution failure,
check the owning cwd, specific alias destination, and installed dependency
closure before changing compiler roots or alias scope.

A config/source handoff or historical donor test and type results do not prove
the current receiver's test, type, CI, or runtime outcome.

## When To Use This Page

Use this page for orientation. Use the DevOps pages for the runbook you actually need
while operating the system.


### Learn preview build validation

The trusted manual `vercel-preview-learn.yaml` workflow builds the checked-out
`preview_ref` with a 35-minute timeout and the existing two-task Turbo limit.
It records a `build` marker using `git rev-parse HEAD`, rather than the main
workflow dispatch SHA. It does not deploy the artifacts. Learn build markers
cannot advance the successful deployment baseline; existing Platform marker
compatibility remains unchanged. A successful build proves compilation, while
actual-device validation and deployment are separate gates.

Focused checks: `node --test scripts/ci/learn-preview-build.test.js
scripts/ci/github-deployment-markers.test.js scripts/ci/release-workflows.test.js`.
